practical.title: Linked Lists in C — Implement and Fix insert_at_end
practical.summary: Progressively inspect, fix, extend, and verify a singly linked list in C by focusing on the insert_at_end function. Four scaffolded scenes guide observation, a targeted bug fix, experimentation with edge cases, and a verification/extension step.
practical.sourceActivity: Linked Lists in C — Implement and Fix insert_at_end

coachingPrompts: What do you predict will happen before you run it?
What evidence shows that your change worked?
Can you explain the result in your own words?

teachingPlaylist.title: Scene 1 — Observe & Understand the Starter Code (baseline run)
teachingPlaylist.learningGoal: Understand Scene 1 — Observe & Understand the Starter Code (baseline run).
teachingPlaylist.narratorScript: Connect: We'll run the supplied C program to observe its current behavior. Explain the Node struct (an int data and a pointer next). Point out insert_at_head (it creates a new node, sets new_node arrow next to head, returns new head). Observe: run the program to see that head insertions worked but end insertions don’t appear. Pause: predict why new end values might be missing. Change: none yet. Test: run and read the printed lists. Explain: note which lines in insert_at_end are commented as BUG.

teachingPlaylist.title: Scene 2 — Modify & Experiment: Fix the 1-2-line bug
teachingPlaylist.learningGoal: Understand Scene 2 — Modify & Experiment: Fix the 1-2-line bug.
teachingPlaylist.narratorScript: Change: Edit insert_at_end and set new_node->next = NULL and then link current->next = new_node. Explain why new_node->next must be NULL and why linking the last node is essential. Test: recompile and run — expect 40 and 50 to appear in the printed list. Explain the difference from the baseline.

teachingPlaylist.title: Scene 3 — Build & Integrate: Experiment with edge cases
teachingPlaylist.learningGoal: Understand Scene 3 — Build & Integrate: Experiment with edge cases.
teachingPlaylist.narratorScript: Connect: We already fixed append for normal cases. Now experiment: change main to append to an empty list, append negative numbers, and append many nodes. Observe output each time. Test: run after each small change. Explain: confirm there are no cycles (no infinite loops) and the printed lists reflect your changes.

teachingPlaylist.title: Scene 4 — Verify & Extend: Tests and a small extension idea
teachingPlaylist.learningGoal: Understand Scene 4 — Verify & Extend: Tests and a small extension idea.
teachingPlaylist.narratorScript: Verify: recompile and run main.c to confirm all printed outputs match expected (head insertions, end insertions, empty list insertion). Extend: we will describe insert_after(head, target, value) — a function that finds a node with data equal to target and inserts a new node immediately after it. Sketch the steps and run a suggested quick manual test by editing main to call the new function. Recap and encourage next practice.
